title: Transport of system arrows to compatible pullback families
statement: Let X be a scheme and let T_n be schemes with maps i_n:T_n to T_(n+1). Let j_n:T_n to X be closed immersions. Put L_n=j_n^* and P_n=i_n^*, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let c_n,d_n:L_(n+1) followed by P_n isomorphic to L_n be arbitrary natural comparison isomorphisms. Let R:Coh(X) to CoherentThickeningSystem(T,i) be a functor, where Coh(X) is the full subcategory of coherent modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and system arrows are compatible component families [def-weil-pbc-coherent-thickening-system]. Suppose natural evaluation isomorphisms r_n:R followed by evaluation_n isomorphic to restriction L_n satisfy comparison_(R F),n followed by r_n,F = P_n(r_(n+1),F) followed by d_n,F for every coherent F and n. For coherent F,G there is an equivalence from Hom(R G,R F) to families v_n:L_n G to L_n F satisfying c_n,G followed by v_n = P_n(v_(n+1)) followed by c_n,F. The equivalence sends R(w) to the family L_n(w) for every coherent-module arrow w:G to F. No formal-completion system occurs in this statement.

source.place: Remark 088F (compatible systems) and Lemma 087T (closed-immersion full faithfulness); elementary categorical transport extracted from the completion dictionary plan

proof.text: Conjugate each system arrow component a_n by r_n,G inverse on the left and r_n,F on the right. Use hr for F and G to translate compatibility into the equation for d_n. The inverse conjugations reconstruct the arrow; the inverse laws hold componentwise by the isomorphism identities and proof irrelevance.

For each closed immersion j_n, choose its tensor-pullback adjunction. The counit is invertible by closedImmersion_pushforward_fullyFaithful, and the left triangle identity makes the pulled-back unit invertible. Conjugating the component of a natural automorphism alpha of j_n^* at j_n,*N by the counit defines a natural automorphism beta of the identity on modules on T_n. Naturality against the unit gives beta_(j_n^*M)=alpha_M. Hence alpha_G commutes with every map j_n^*G to j_n^*F. Apply this to alpha=d_n.symm followed by c_n and cancel alpha_F to identify the c_n and d_n compatibility equations.

Combine the componentwise conjugation bijection with the identification of family subtypes. Naturality of r identifies the family of R.map w with the pullbacks of w; the proof of family compatibility is naturality of c.

proof_origin.place: Categorical conjugation and comparison independence argument expanded from Remark 088F and Lemma 087T; no Grothendieck existence used

theorem thickeningSystem_hom_transport
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {T : ℕ → Scheme.{u}} {i : ∀ n, T n ⟶ T (n + 1)}
    (j : ∀ n, T n ⟶ X) (hj : ∀ n, IsClosedImmersion (j n))
    (c d : ∀ n, Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j (n + 1)) ⋙
      Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (i n) ≅ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j n))
    (R : CoherentModules X ⥤ CoherentThickeningSystem T i)
    (r : ∀ n, R ⋙ CoherentThickeningSystem.evaluation T i n ≅
      ObjectProperty.ι (RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace) ⋙
        Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j n))
    (hr : ∀ (F : CoherentModules X) (n : ℕ),
      ((R.obj F).comparison n).hom ≫ (r n).hom.app F =
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (i n)).map ((r (n + 1)).hom.app F) ≫
          (d n).hom.app F.obj)
    (F G : CoherentModules X) :
    ∃ e : (R.obj G ⟶ R.obj F) ≃
      {v : ∀ n, (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j n)).obj G.obj ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j n)).obj F.obj |
        ∀ n, (c n).hom.app G.obj ≫ v n =
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (i n)).map (v (n + 1)) ≫ (c n).hom.app F.obj},
      ∀ w : G ⟶ F, e (R.map w) =
        ⟨fun n ↦ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (j n)).map w.hom,
          fun n ↦ ((c n).hom.naturality w.hom).symm⟩
